name: Sacristy of the Cartuja
aka: Real Monasterio de Nuestra Señora de la Asunción de la Cartuja

dates.altered: The monastery was founded in 1516 and built through the 16th, 17th and 18th centuries; the community was expelled at the exclaustration of 1835.
dates.note: The node's exemplar dates the sacristy 1732-1747 to Luis de Arevalo and Luis Cabello. The article's infobox says the sacristy is 'de autor desconocido' and gives no date for it; its construction field covers 'Siglos XVI, XVII y XVIII' for the whole monastery. Both are recorded and neither is resolved.

refs.note: THE PAGE CONTRADICTS ITSELF ABOUT THE DATE AND BOTH READINGS ARE CARRIED. Its infobox prints 'Identificador RI-51-0000582' and 'Declaración 6 de abril de 1931'; its text says the monastery 'fue declarado monumento histórico-artístico perteneciente al Tesoro Artístico Nacional mediante decreto de 3 de junio de 1931'. Two dates two months apart on one page; neither is changed.

quotes.text: De exuberante decoración, sus espacios más célebres son la iglesia, la sacristía, de autor desconocido, y el sagrario que es obra del maestro Francisco Hurtado Izquierdo y cuenta con una impresionante cúpula pintada por Antonio Palomino.
Aunque mezcla diversos estilos, representa una de las cumbres de la arquitectura barroca española.
Portada, es del siglo XVI y de estilo plateresco.
quotes.page: Spanish Wikipedia, section 'Descripción', in the list of the building's parts

note: Tranche 3, 5 Sep 2026. NO MEASUREMENT IS RECORDED and the sacristy the node names is attributed to nobody by its own source. The third quote is kept because it is a fact against the tidy story: the doorway of the most extreme Churrigueresque interior in Spain is a sixteenth-century PLATERESQUE portada, so one building in this cluster carries two of these seven nodes in one elevation.
